title: Subtree of Another Tree
statement: You get a big binary tree and a smaller pattern tree. Say whether the big tree contains a node whose whole subtree, shape and values, is exactly the pattern. Matching only part of a subtree does not count.

example.caption: The node 4 in the big tree, with its children 1 and 2, is an exact copy of the pattern.

idea.sentence: Try every node of the big tree as a starting point, and at each one ask the Same Tree question against the pattern.

jargon.plain: A node plus everything below it, all the way to the leaves. You cannot stop early.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the big tree and the pattern, each a level-order array with null for a missing child

compare.bruteLabel: Try every node with a full comparison (worst case)
compare.optimalLabel: Same, but each comparison stops at the first difference

rows.name: Try every node + Same Tree
rows.note: n start points. Each comparison walks up to m nodes. It usually quits far sooner.

rows.name: Serialize both, search the text
rows.note: Faster in theory with a linear string search, but it needs careful empty-spot markers.

fast.takeaway: The simple version reuses Same Tree and is fast enough in practice because most comparisons fail on the first node.

stages.title: Base cases
stages.note: An empty pattern fits anywhere. If the big tree runs out, there is no match down this path.

stages.title: Try matching here
stages.note: Check whether the subtree starting at this node is identical to the pattern, using the same pair-walk as Same Tree.

stages.title: Search deeper
stages.note: No match here, so try the left child, then the right child, as new starting points.

edges.title: Pattern is the whole tree
edges.why: The root itself is a starting point, and it matches.

edges.title: Extra node below
edges.why: Node 4 matches the pattern at the top, but node 2 has an extra child 0. A subtree includes everything below.

edges.title: Same values, wrong shape
edges.why: Matching values is not enough. The shape must match too.

edges.title: Pattern larger than the tree
edges.why: The pattern has a node the big tree cannot supply.

gotchas.text: Do not stop at the first matching root value. 4 matching 4 only means this is a candidate. The full comparison decides.
Run the comparison at every node, not only at nodes whose value equals the pattern's root. It is simpler and cannot miss a match.
The comparison is Same Tree, not 'pattern is contained in': a leaf in the pattern must also be a leaf in the big tree.
Use ||, not |, so a found match returns immediately without searching the right side.
Check subRoot == nil before root == nil. If both are nil the answer is true, because an empty pattern always matches.

recap.key: At every node of the big tree, run the Same Tree check against the pattern. If none matches, the answer is false.
recap.complexity: Time O(n * m). Space O(h) call stack.
moves: Empty pattern: true. Empty big tree: false
If the tree here equals the pattern, return true
